The live file is digest-routine/sources.json, which is gitignored because accounts[].email must hold the real Gmail address for STEP 1.1's connector cross-check to work. _accounts_comment: The inboxes the routine scans. As of 2026-09-08 this is a SINGLE-ACCOUNT setup by user instruction: <redacted> is the only source. A previous account (<redacted>) was retired on 2026-09-08 and deliberately removed - do not re-add it, and do not report it as missing. STEP 1 still discovers connectors at run time and reconciles against this list: an account here with no live connector is reported as de-authorized rather than silently skipped, and a live connector missing from here is treated as newly added (appended with backfill '30d' / backfillState 'pending', giving it one catch-up pass over its last month before the normal unread + last-7-days window). Authorize a connector and the next run does the rest. Order matters only for tie-breaking when one newsletter reaches two inboxes: the first-listed account's permalink is cited.

drop._comment: Checked first. A match here means the message is never fetched, even from a Tier A sender.
subject_patterns: you shared some google account data

keyword_pass: GPT OR Claude OR Gemini OR Anthropic OR OpenAI
"model release" OR benchmark OR eval OR RLHF OR fine-tuning

tldr_rules._comment: TLDR sends two editions a day from dan@tldrnewsletter.com. Distinguish them by the header line in the body, NOT by size or arrival time.
tldr_rules.keep_edition: Prefer the edition whose body header reads 'TLDR AI <date>' and take it under the section rules below. Do NOT discard the general tech edition unseen: scan it and lift only items that would have qualified in the AI edition (a released model, tool, benchmark, method or infrastructure change relevant to an AI engineer) and that the AI edition has not already covered. Some genuine AI releases land only in the general edition - Claude Fable 5.1's GA on 2026-09-02 is the worked example. Everything else in that edition - consumer hardware, executive moves, regulatory filings, market news - is dropped.

conditional_sections.rule: Keep an item only if it changes what an AI engineer can build, run, or rely on - a released artifact, a benchmark result, a method, a capability claim, or an infrastructure change. Drop pure market and finance items (IPO timing, bond markets, share prices) and executive/personnel news.

always_drop: the referral / 'get free TLDR swag' block
consumer gadget and non-AI tech news
tldr_rules.rationale: User instruction 2026-09-07: AI news from an AI engineer's perspective only - no deals, no marketing, developer-relevant news only.
